comparisons.peer_topic: CHIPS Act-funded U.S. fab expansion plans and timeline
comparisons.peer_summary: Plans to invest in two U.S. fab facilities were announced following the CHIPS Act: construction began in Boise, Idaho in October 2023 with output projected in 2027, and a second facility in Clay, New York is expected to begin site preparation in 2025 with production ramping in the latter half of the decade, intended to meet future wafer capacity demand.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Micron disclose major long-term manufacturing expansion plans supported by or influenced by the U.S. CHIPS Act, though the stages and specifics differ. Intel describes plans to expand operations in Arizona, New Mexico, and Oregon, and invest in a new leading-edge facility in Ohio, but notes that some longer-term projects like new advanced packaging facilities are currently on hold or slowed due to uncertainty. In contrast, Micron details active progress on two U.S. fab facilities announced under the CHIPS Act: construction began in Boise, Idaho with output projected for 2027, and a second facility in Clay, New York is expected to begin site preparation in 2025. Micron presents these expansions as key to meeting future demand, whereas Intel highlights pauses in certain long-term projects alongside its expansion commitments.

sentences.text: These plans include expanding existing operations in Arizona, New Mexico, and Oregon, and investing in a new leading-edge manufacturing facility in Ohio.

They may also include longer-term projects, certain of which we have currently put on hold or slowed the completion of, including a new leading-edge manufacturing facility, a new assembly and test facility, and a new advanced packaging facility, among others.

Following the enactment of the U.S. CHIPS and Science Act of 2022 ("CHIPS Act"), we announced plans to invest in two leading-edge memory manufacturing fab facilities in the United States, based on CHIPS Act support through grants and investment tax credits.
As part of this plan, in September 2022, we broke ground on a leading-edge memory manufacturing fab in Boise, Idaho.
In addition, in October 2022, we announced plans to build a second leading-edge DRAM manufacturing facility, consisting of up to four fabs to be built over the next 20-plus years, in Clay, New York.

We expect these new fabs to be key to meeting our requirements for additional wafer capacity starting in the second half of the decade and beyond, in line with industry demand trends and to maintain an objective of stable bit share.
